scope: Gameplay-facing material and texture intent, raster loading, texture-slot binding, UV/vertex-stream and render-state inputs, semantically consumed lighting activation, and the boundary to RenderWare/D3D implementation. Original third-party internals are treated as replaceable implementation; content identity, material identity, slot association, state ordering, and draw inputs are preserved as contracts.

boundaries.boundary: Gameplay material and texture intent: cell/content resource selection, material IDs, and texture references
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Simulator::Cell::cCellGFX::PreloadResources and cCellGFX::PreloadCellResource; cCellGFX::AddPreloadedTexture for preload insertion
boundaries.original_callee: Simulator::Cell::cCellGFX::AddPreloadedTexture; cCellGFX::PreloadCellResource and cCellGFX::PreloadPopulateResource; resource/material manager calls reached by the preload path
parameters: material identity or Texture* selected by content data
model, effect, populate, creature, and texture association
outputs: texture, model, effect, or creature references stored for display
boundaries.lifetime: Stage/display lifetime. Content and resource managers own the referenced records; cCellGFX retains the stage association until the Cell presentation is replaced or disposed.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The original decompilation has null guards and allocation fallback but no explicit status return. Missing-resource and unsupported-content behavior is not fully resolved. The triage record is static-only and explicitly not runtime-validated.
boundaries.timing_order: Resource and texture preload precedes StartDisplay; the resulting associations are consumed when the Cell world/layers become visible.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Gameplay/content material intent is a stable material ID plus texture keys and slot associations, not a RenderWare MaterialShader or Raster pointer.
boundaries.notes: The material-ID and texture-reference structure is a clean-room content contract. The original AddPreloadedTexture body has heavily type-ambiguous decompiler aliases, so the exact collection ownership and material-to-slot relation remain inferred. This boundary is semantic content selection, not a request to reconstruct RW object layouts.

boundaries.boundary: Stable material ID to shader/material definition lookup
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Graphics material selection/loading path; the direct caller is not present in the committed decompilation export
outputs: nullptr when no list entry matches
state_changed: DAT_017186d4 caches the last matching MaterialShader pointer
boundaries.lifetime: The material registry owns the records; a returned handle is valid only while its material-manager records remain alive. The lookup cache does not establish a new ownership lifetime.
boundaries.failure_semantics: A missing ID returns nullptr and does not visibly report an error code. The cache is updated only on a match.
boundaries.timing_order: Resolve a material ID before binding compiled state, active shader data, and the draw submission.
boundaries.openspore_concept: A stable MaterialId resolves to a material definition containing texture-slot bindings, shader family, and constants.
boundaries.notes: The function is an engine-side lookup, but the ID-to-definition association is content semantics. Preserve the ID and definition contract, not the original linked-list pointer, DAT cache, or calling convention.

boundaries.boundary: Graphics manager service roots used to reach material, texture, renderer, and lighting implementations
boundaries.gameplay_caller: cCellGFX::Initialize/StartDisplay and material/texture/draw code that first obtains a Graphics service
boundaries.lifetime: Process/service-manager lifetime. These accessors do not own a per-draw material or texture and do not create a new resource lifetime.
boundaries.failure_semantics: They return the stored global pointer; an uninitialized service can therefore yield null or a later invalid virtual call. No explicit initialization error is returned by the wrappers.
boundaries.timing_order: The accessor is called immediately before a service virtual method such as lighting-world selection, renderer-layer creation, or material/texture operations.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Service discovery is an implementation convenience; the semantic contract is the injected manager interface and its typed operations.
boundaries.notes: These are thin global-service accessors, not gameplay material data. Do not reproduce DAT globals or the original 32-bit vtable layout in OpenSpore.

boundaries.boundary: Raster record decoding and GPU texture upload
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Cell/resource preload path obtains a raster record; a later material draw consumes the resulting texture resource
boundaries.original_callee: RenderWare::Raster::Create, CreateRaster, Extract, and D3D9AddToUnmanagedList; the Graphics texture-manager implementation around those calls
parameters: raster envelope fields: width, height, mip count, and FOURCC
state_changed: resource texture cache or raster state
GPU texture image, view, and sampler state after upload
boundaries.lifetime: The source record belongs to content/resource lifetime; decoded images and GPU textures are valid until their explicit destroy operation. The original RW raster lifetime is not exposed as a gameplay contract.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The original Raster bodies are not locally decompiled, so their failure contract is unresolved. OpenSpore's clean-room decoder returns false with an error for truncated envelopes, unsupported FOURCC, zero mip count, invalid layer splitting, or a mip slice beyond the record.
boundaries.timing_order: Decode the asset before texture creation, then upload before material binding and before the first draw that samples it.
boundaries.openspore_concept: The semantic asset boundary is a content texture asset with dimensions, mip data, format, and a stable resource key; the RW Raster object and D3D upload are replaceable infrastructure.

evidence.symbol: derived raster layer count and DXT5 mip chain
raster/DXT5 oracle and C++ port plan
Vulkan texture descriptor and sampler binding

boundaries.notes: Raster format and texture resource identity are strong asset-contract evidence. The current OpenSpore upload is a single-level RGBA8 approximation; the clean-room decoder can expose mips, but the current IRenderer createTexture contract does not carry a mip chain.

boundaries.gameplay_caller: Material submission/CompiledState::Load path after gameplay/content has selected the material; indirect from cCellGFX texture preload
outputs: SetRaster has no visible return value
GetRaster returns the Raster bound to the requested slot or nullptr
state_changed: slot binding is updated only when the requested raster differs
boundaries.lifetime: A compiled state and its raster references live with the material/resource lifetime. Slot pointers must not outlive the referenced raster or compiled-state object.
boundaries.failure_semantics: GetRaster returns nullptr when the slot is absent. SetRaster has no explicit validation/error path in the decompilation; malformed or mismatched slot state is not characterized.
boundaries.timing_order: Load or create the material, bind rasters to material slots, then submit the active material and draw. The slot binding is semantic state even though the table walker is RW implementation detail.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Material definitions own stable texture-slot bindings; the renderer resolves slots to backend texture handles.
boundaries.notes: The exact RW slot table layout is not reconstructed. Preserve stable slot indices and binding results; replace the table walker and raster pointer with typed material/texture handles.

boundaries.boundary: Current-frame active texture, sampler, and shader-constant state
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Graphics material/draw submission path; exact original gameplay caller is not present in the committed decompilation export
parameters: texture stage or slot and raster/texture handle for SetTexture; exact original signature is not locally exported
short index, void* value, and bool overrideIfEqual for SetShaderData
shader-data index and value payload for backend registration
outputs: updated shader-data records consumed by a subsequent draw
boundaries.lifetime: Texture/material resources outlive the frame; active texture and shader-data state is frame-scoped and is replaced or refreshed as draws change materials.
boundaries.failure_semantics: SetShaderData visibly no-ops when the active shader is absent or the current shader-data count is zero and has no status return. The committed export does not contain the SetTexture body, so sampler override and invalid-texture behavior remain unresolved.
boundaries.timing_order: Set material and shader constants/textures before the draw; the active shader's vertex declaration and state are then read during mesh submission. State transitions should remain ordered even if Vulkan descriptors or push constants replace D3D calls.
boundaries.openspore_concept: A per-draw material binding contract containing texture slots, sampler policy, shader family, and constants; the backend owns descriptor/pipeline mechanics.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IMaterialBindings + IRenderStateCache + IPipelineState; bindTexture, setShaderData, and submit
boundaries.notes: The active-state implementation is backend state, but slot/constant ordering is a compatibility contract. The current OpenSpore MaterialState contains only lightDir and ambient; it does not yet carry the original shader ID or multi-slot texture bindings.

boundaries.boundary: UV/vertex declaration, stream rebinding, index scope, and indexed draw inputs
boundaries.gameplay_caller: RenderWare::Mesh::Render draw helper reached by model and terrain submission; exact gameplay callers are not in the local decompilation export
boundaries.original_callee: RenderWare::VertexDescriptionBase::LoadDeclaration, RenderWare::Mesh::SetIndexBuffer, RenderWare::Mesh::SetIndicesCount, and the active-shader vertex-declaration virtual
parameters: vertex declaration elements: stream, offset, position/normal/texcoord usage, type, and stride
outputs: indexed draw transition; the actual DrawIndexedPrimitive is issued by the caller
state_changed: surplus stream unbinding when the active stream count shrinks
index-buffer state in DAT_016f85a8 and DAT_016f8afc
boundaries.lifetime: Vertex and index resources live with their mesh/draw resource; stream and index bindings are current renderer state. Modern mesh handles may be destroyed after frame submission, not before GPU use completes.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The RW helper returns early when stream binding reports failure and when the index-scope check fails. SetIndicesCount has no visible error return. The exact device-wrapper error mapping is implementation detail.
boundaries.timing_order: After material/active-shader state is selected, bind the declared streams, unbind surplus streams, validate and bind indices, then issue the indexed draw. UV values are consumed through the declared texcoord stream.
boundaries.openspore_concept: A mesh draw contract with vertex layout, UV/normal/position inputs, index buffer, topology, and explicit draw ordering; no RW stream cache or D3D vertex declaration object is exposed.
boundaries.notes: The state-transition order is stronger evidence than the exact D3D wrapper calls. UV is a semantic vertex input; D3D vertex declarations, RW object fields, and stream-cache globals are replaceable implementation.

boundaries.boundary: Lighting-world and shadow-state activation at Cell display entry
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Simulator::Cell::cCellGFX::StartDisplay invoked during Cell mode entry
boundaries.original_callee: Graphics::ILightingManager::Get followed by ILightingManager::GetLightingWorld; Graphics::IShadowWorld::Get followed by IShadowWorld::Reset; cCellGFX world-handle virtual calls
parameters: lighting-world handles from PTR_PTR_015a841c, PTR_PTR_015a8420, PTR_PTR_015a8424, and PTR_PTR_015a8428
lighting selectors 2, 5, 13, and 24 as observed call arguments
cCellGFX world handles for display enable/disable
outputs: enabled or disabled cCellGFX world/layer state
boundaries.lifetime: Lighting and shadow state is tied to the Cell display/world lifetime and is reset or replaced when the stage changes. The original lighting object ownership is not inferred.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The decompilation shows no explicit return value or recoverable error path for the lighting calls. Invalid manager/world pointers would fail through the virtual-call path rather than a typed status.
boundaries.timing_order: After Cell GFX world/layer creation and preload, StartDisplay selects lighting worlds, enables/disables world handles, resets shadow state, and opens display-related state before the visible frame.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Stage presentation state must preserve world identity, activation order, and shadow reset. The actual light color, intensity, fog, and D3D fixed-function pixel behavior are presentation-only visuals, not gameplay simulation state.
